summary: This is a sound, rules-clean port of four Triton GEMMs, each measured faster at exactly these shapes in muse_bf16_proj. The expected headline is only about +0.7-1.0% geomean, inside one run's CI, so the result has to be read from the per-GEMM top_kernels rows and the per-shape rows. The two real risks are that a verbatim copy of bf16_proj's cfg-keyed guards KeyErrors or silently falls back to cuBLAS, and that the 128-CTA, 160 KB-smem Triton pooler starves the side-stream router.
justification: The mechanism is plausible. bf16_proj measured each kernel faster than nvjet+splitKreduce on the same weight shapes (pooler [4096,8192], qkv_gate [2304,8192], o [8192,1024], unpooler slice [1024 rows of 4096-stride]), also under a cold L2. Each one also removes a graph node, and LESSONS puts that at ~2-4 us per nvjet+splitKreduce pair against ~0.3 us per Triton launch. FINDINGS supports the size of the target. On master the nvjet 128x8 splitK row is 31.9-32.8 us at decode_1 and verify_1 (20.7-21.5% of the sliding and full shapes). At decode_16 the nvjet 64x16 and 128x16 splitK rows add up to ~46 us. The pooler alone runs at ~1.4x its ~14 us floor (21 us), so ~2 us per GEMM is realistic. The expected directions match the gates: T=1, 8 and 16 are routed, and T=32/128/256 stay on cuBLAS. The magnitudes are a little understated in relative terms, because they divide by SGLang's 173-182 us rather than master's 146-157 us. In absolute terms: decode_1 about -4.5 us (+2.9-3.1%), verify_1 -2.5-3 us (+1.2-1.4%), decode_16 sliding -2 us (+0.9%) and full -2 us (+0.6%). Over six equally weighted loads that is about +0.8% on the geomean, below the ~1.5% one run can resolve. Expect a 'neutral' headline even if every GEMM wins. WEAKEST LINK: the pooler's 21.2->19.2 us win was measured with the pooler alone on the GPU. Here it runs on the main stream concurrently with the side-stream router: fp32 F.linear gemv at T=1, two hi/lo torch.mm plus FusedMuseSparkRouting at T=8/16. The Triton pooler is one wave of 128 CTAs at 4 stages x (64x256 + 16x256) x 2 B = 160 KB of smem each, so one CTA per SM fills 128 of 132 SMs for its whole duration. That can serialise the router behind the pooler, where today it fits under the ~22-25 us nvjet pooler (DECISIONS 092231Z). If that happens, the pooler's own row drops while the shape time rises by up to the router branch (~9-18 us). qkv, o and the unpooler run on the main stream with nothing beside them, so their bf16_proj numbers should carry over almost exactly (LESSONS: Triton times reproduce within ~1%).
confounders: sglang-pipeline-parity-router-hilo-m8: it sets what runs beside the pooler. At T=1 that is the fp32 F.linear gemv; at T>=2 it is two bf16 hi/lo torch.mm on the side stream. How well the 128-CTA Triton pooler overlaps the router depends on that branch's SM and smem demand. A pooler-row gain with a flat or worse shape time would be an interaction effect, not the kernel. With the starter's fp32 router at T=8 the branch would be longer and contention worse. This is the only landed item that can make the measured effect differ from the change's own.

post-expert-norm-triton-small-t: it is not a timing confounder, but it now produces the unpooler slice's input at T<32 (contiguous bf16 [T,4096], so the stride(1)==1 guard passes). It also removed ~9 launches, so the unpooler's graph-node saving is now a larger share of a shorter shape. If it were absent, x would come from fused_post_expert_norm_weighted_sum, whose output strides should be confirmed. The gain direction would not change.

fa3-hdim128-head-pairing-batched: only the decode_16 full row overlaps (batch>1 full layers). The o GEMM's input is the FusedRMSNormGate output after the un-pad, a fresh contiguous tensor, so the o path sees the same input as unpaired. No interaction is expected.
marlin-block-m-cap-16: it affects only T=128/256 (verify_16/32), which are this hypothesis's cuBLAS controls. It is disjoint and does not confound.
interference: No companion is warranted. A gain is not ambiguous: the replaced kernels have their own top_kernels rows (the nvjet 128x8 / 64x16 / 128x16 splitK and splitKreduce rows should vanish at T<=16, replaced by _bf16_splitk_kernel, _qkv_splitk_sem_kernel and _pooler_skinny_kernel rows), so each GEMM's contribution can be read per shape. A loss is mostly readable too. If the Triton rows are faster than the nvjet rows they replace but a shape's time rose, the pooler/router overlap is to blame, because nothing else in the change runs concurrently. The only companion that would sharpen this is a control keeping the pooler on _gemm while routing qkv/o/unpooler to Triton. It is worth minting only as a follow-up if the run shows that signature, not before. Checks are spent and this goes out as a scored submit, so spending a second scored attempt in advance on a ~1% effect is poor value. ab-revert of the router change is not meaningful: reverting it changes the T=8 router to the fp32 SIMT GEMM and moves the critical path, so it answers a different question.
rules_flags: No rule problem in the design. Weights stay BF16 and are read in place (the unpooler slice by row stride, no copy). Accumulation is fp32 with one bf16 rounding at the store, the same output precision as cuBLAS. The split-K reduce sums in a fixed order. Routing reads only cfg['tokens'] and shapes. There are no host syncs. Workspaces and counters are allocated in prepare() and hold nothing derived from data. Every partial is written and read in the same launch under the same row mask, and nothing from an earlier call can reach the output. torch.empty outputs inside kernel_fn match what master already does.

CORRECTNESS / implementability, highest risk for a scored submit: bf16_proj's guards (_pooler_shape_ok, _qkv_route_ok, _unpool_shape_ok, _o_skinny_applies) read cfg['m'], cfg['n'] and cfg['k']. decode_layer's Config has no such keys, so a verbatim copy raises KeyError on the first test. Copy the kernels and _*_forward launchers verbatim, but rewrite each gate from cfg['tokens'] and x.shape and weight shape. Make the gates assert their preconditions rather than fall back silently, or a stride or dtype mismatch quietly measures master. Print the route table once in prepare().

Copy only the m<=16 paths. bf16_proj master now also carries _bf16_swapab_kernel, _swapab_prepare and SWAPAB_* (bf16-m32-swapab-wgmma-triton, 1.198x). Pulling those in would silently change the T=32 decode_32 'control' shapes.

Tested T values that reach the new paths: 1 (ctx10, ctx3000, the scored-like full test), 8 (batch 8; batch 1 q_len 8), 9 (batch 9: qkv/o/pooler Triton, unpooler on full cuBLAS since T>8), and 16 (batch 16; batch 2 q_len 8). T=24/32/33/40 stay on cuBLAS. Masking makes every M in 1..16 valid, and prepare() warms 1..16 (1..8 for the unpooler), so the timed call never compiles. Keep the post-warm-up synchronize and zero_() of all three cnt buffers.
open_questions: Will the 128-CTA, 1-CTA-per-SM Triton pooler leave the side-stream router to run after it, rather than beside it, at T=8/16? Compare decode_16 and verify_1 shape time minus kernel sum against master's. If it does, a pooler kernel at 3 stages (two CTAs per SM, ~120 KB) or with fewer CTAs is the follow-up.

The expected geomean gain (~+0.8%) is inside one run's CI. Is a scored attempt the right vehicle, or should bf16_proj's m=32 swap-AB wins (pooler +9.3%, o +4.1%, qkv +3.6% at m=32) be ported into this same run, so that decode_32 (T=32, both layers) also moves and the headline clears noise? That would drop decode_32 as a control. It is the caller's call: as written the hypothesis is clean but probably reads neutral.

Confirm that attn_input (a judge input), the o_norm_gate output and ffn_input from attn_boundary have stride(1)==1 and a 16-divisible stride(0) at every tested T. If any is a non-contiguous view, the asserting gate catches it in the tests rather than in a silent fallback.
